Web 客户端将别名和头像保存在 localStorage，并覆盖匹配的侧栏 DOM。
只读固定 README、清单、宿主空入口与客户端存储及显示路径；未运行 DSH、浏览器或截图。
DSH Web 客户端插件；具体宿主 DOM 兼容未实测。

"content": "# dsh-accountdisplayname-edit Replaces the sidebar account label — the phone number, email, or account name DeepSeek Harness shows at the bottom-left — and the avatar above it, with a name and image you choose, so screenshots do not expose the original. The edit entry is a new **Edit display name** row in the account menu, the one you open by clicking that label. The dialog it opens holds both the avatar and the name. ## What it does - Replaces the account label text in the sidebar footer with a display name you set. - Replaces the launcher avatar with an image you pick from a local file. - Adds an **Edit display name** / **编辑显示名称** row to the account menu, directly under Settings. - Opens one editor dialog for both: pick or clear an avatar, type a name, then Save, Cancel, or Use default. `Enter` saves, `Esc` cancels. - Both edits are drafts until Save — Cancel leaves the sidebar untouched. - Saving an empty value restores the account's own text; clearing the avatar restores the account's own avatar. - A picked image is centre-cropped square, downscaled to 128×128 and re-encoded, so the stored copy stays in the low tens of KB. - Stores both per browser in `localStorage`, under `dsh.account-display-name-edit.alias` and `dsh.account-display-name-edit.avatar`. - Display only. The account, the credentials and the profile are never read or changed, and the plugin makes no network requests of its own. ## Requirements Built and verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`. The account launcher and `Menu` DOM it targets — `data-signed-out`, the `_avatar` / `_label` spans, the portaled `div[role="menu"]` with its `role="presentation"` viewport and `itemIcon` / `itemLabel` rows — is unchanged in `0.2.1-rc.2`, which this package was checked against. The host half imports nothing and the browser half fails soft, so a build whose DOM has moved on degrades to "no override, no extra row" rather than an error — see [Compatibility](#compatibility). ## Install ### From the desktop app The `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application, so install it there through the app's own plugin surface (Settings → Plugins, or `dshmarket`); the CLI refuses that profile by design. ### From the CLI, for any profile the app does not own ```sh dsh plugin --profile add github:AomiRaku/dsh-accountDisplayName-edit # or from npm, which skips the git fetch and build approval entirely: dsh plugin --profile add dsh-accountdisplayname-edit ``` There is **no build step and no `prepare` script**: the browser half is committed as `lib/client.js`, so pnpm never asks for build approval and the install is a plain file copy. ### Manually, which is exactly what the commands above do 1. Put the package where the profile resolves its bundles — `/profiles//node_modules/dsh-accountdisplayname-edit`. A directory junction/symlink to a checkout works. 2. Add this to `/profiles//cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - insert: - id: account-display-name-edit name: dsh-accountdisplayname-edit ``` That patch layer is watched, so it applies live — no restart needed. ## Use 1. Click the account row at the bottom of the sidebar. 2. Choose **Edit display name**. 3. Optionally click **Choose image…** and pick a PNG / JPG / WebP; the round preview shows the cropped result. **Clear avatar** goes back to the account's own avatar. 4. Type the name you want. Save an empty value to go back to the account's own text. 5. Click **Save**. Nothing changes until you do. ## Screenshots The account menu, with the **Edit display name** row added under Settings, and the chosen name and avatar on the launcher below it: ![The account menu with the Edit display name row](assets/screenshot-1.png) The editor dialog: avatar preview, name field, and Save / Cancel / Use default: ![The editor dialog](assets/screenshot-2.png) ## Uninstall Remove the insert from `cordis.patch.yml` and delete the package directory. The stored name and avatar stay in the browser's `localStorage` until you clear them; the plugin writes nothing else. ## How it works A dual-face plugin whose host half does almost nothing. - **Host half — `lib/index.js`.** Deliberately import-free. Its only job is to be a Loader entry, so the host's client-module scanner reads `dsh.client` from `package.json` and serves `./client` to the browser. With no dependencies and no `peerDependencies`, it cannot fail to load because of a missing, renamed or version-mismatched peer package. - **Browser half — `lib/client.js`.** A hand-written single-file bundle, already in the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` form the module system serves verbatim, so the package needs no build. It requires only `react`, which the shell seeds as a platform module — which is why `react` is not a dependency either. ### Why the menu row is done in the DOM `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-account` renders that menu from a hard-coded `items` array, and its only slot (`settings.launcher`, a `single` slot) is the launcher row itself. Occupying that slot would delete 设置 / 意见反馈 / 退出登录, which this plugin must not do. There is no menu-item slot to add to. So the row is appended to the **open** menu's list, cloned from a shipped row — it therefore inherits that build's exact markup, classes and styling. Appending one node leaves React's own children untouched, and the row is removed with the menu because React never tracked it. Selectors use only stable identifiers, never a hashed CSS-module prefix: - the launcher is `button[aria-haspopup="menu"][data-signed-out]`, an attribute the account component always writes; the text node is found by the `_label` suffix and the avatar by the `_avatar` suffix, with positional fallbacks; - the menu is a `div[role="menu"]` the `Menu` primitive portals to ``, identified as the one that appeared after the launcher was activated. ### How the avatar is replaced The avatar span's real contents are React's — an `` or an initial. Rather than remove them, the plugin paints the picked image as the span's **background** and hides the span's children with one scoped rule: ```css [data-dsh-accountdisplayname-edit-avatar="1"] > * { display: none !important } ``` That is two attribute writes and a background image; no React-owned node is detached, re-parented or replaced, so a later account refresh cannot collide with it. Clearing the avatar removes the attribute and the background, and the real avatar reappears. ### Failing soft Every DOM probe runs inside `try`/`catch`; when a probe misses, the plugin does nothing — it never edits another node and never throws into the shell's plugin loader. Clearing the name hands the account plugin's own text back. The label is written through React's own text node (`nodeValue`, not `textContent`), so later account refreshes stay observable instead of updating a node React no longer owns. ## Compatibility - `dsh.client.immediately: true` is required: the plugin works through side effects registered when its bundle materializes, so it belongs in the boot graph's immediate tier. - No `engines.dsh` range is declared, on purpose. node-semver only admits a prerelease version when some comparator in the range shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple and itself carries a prerelease tag, so any range would silently exclude a later prerelease of the harness — the failure mode the awesome-dsh-plugin contributing guide warns about. Failing soft is the safer contract here. ## Verification ```sh npm install npm test ``` 116 checks against a real DOM (jsdom + React 18.3.1): - `test/dom.test.mjs` — 40 checks: the bundle wrapper contract, `apply()` registration, label replacement, re-application after the account half re-renders, menu-row injection (label, icon, dropped shortcut, insertion position, shipped rows untouched), row activation closing the menu and opening the dialog, save and reset, and disposal. - `test/robustness.test.mjs` — 16 checks over the fail-soft paths: the account row gone entirely, the `_label` class renamed, the collapsed rail where the avatar is the only span, an English locale, a menu rendered before its rows exist, no `document.body`, the account span replaced by a React remount, and disposal after the account row was removed. - `test/avatar.test.mjs` — 28 checks: a stored image painted on the launcher, the scoped stylesheet, the real avatar left intact, the dialog's file input and pick/clear controls, draft-vs-Save semantics for the avatar, a signed-out launcher without an avatar span, a corrupted stored value, and disposal. Picking a file itself is not exercised here: jsdom has no 2D canvas and never decodes images. - `test/edge-cases.test.mjs` — 32 checks over the failure and teardown paths: a disable landing between two frames of the menu poll, a re-enable after a disable while the dialog was open, a name the browser refuses to persist, the collapsed rail before and after it expands, double disposal, re-applying, the menu closing through the launcher's own toggle instead of a document-wide Escape, the dialog's Tab containment and short-window scrolling, the click path performing **zero** document-wide queries while leaving the menu's own opening frame untouched, and a re-created label node, avatar node, or whole launcher button being repainted before the next frame (no flash). It was also verified in a live DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`: the host entry reached `fiberPhase: active`, and the running Web GUI's slot tree listed the plugin's `shell.overlay` entry as active, which means the host served the bundle and the page materialized and ran it. ## Store listing The awesome-dsh-plugin entry is ready to copy: ```text store-entry/data/plugins/AomiRaku__dsh-accountDisplayName-edit.yml -> data/plugins/AomiRaku__dsh-accountDisplayName-edit.yml ``` That one file, added to a fork of [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin), is the whole submission — do not edit the generated READMEs by hand. Screenshots are declared in [`screenshots.json`](screenshots.json) next to `package.json`, which lists two repository-relative images in display order. They live in this repository, so replacing one is a push here — not a new pull request to the list. ```json ["assets/screenshot-1.png", "assets/screenshot-2.png"] ``` ## Known limitations - The menu row and the avatar override depend on the shipped account-menu DOM.
